title: Frozen-Core 20L with Stopband QWOT Initialization and Curvature Penalty
scientific_hypothesis: Fixing the inner 10 layers (8-17) at the empirically-optimized 215.0 nm value while initializing outer 12 layers at quarter-wave optical thickness for the lower stopband center (1450 nm) will reduce compensatory overshoot and improve convergence toward the 0.95 transmission target, with L2 curvature penalty suppressing adjacent-layer thickness oscillations.
design_principle: Defective DBR bandpass filter with frozen core acting as the defect cavity region, outer layers serving as impedance-matching mirrors. Quarter-wave initialization at stopband wavelength provides stronger initial suppression before optimization refines the passband.
proposed_topology: 20 alternating layers: Ta2O5(1)-SiO2(2)-Ta2O5(3)-SiO2(4)-Ta2O5(5)-SiO2(6)-Ta2O5(7)-SiO2(8)-Ta2O5(9)-SiO2(10)-Ta2O5(11)-SiO2(12)-Ta2O5(13)-SiO2(14)-Ta2O5(15)-SiO2(16)-Ta2O5(17)-SiO2(18)-Ta2O5(19)-SiO2(20). Layers 8-17 fixed at 215.0 nm. Layers 1-7 and 18-20 optimized.
soft_objectives: minimize mean transmittance in 1400-1500 nm stopband
minimize mean transmittance in 1600-1700 nm stopband
manufacturing_considerations: 215.0 nm thickness is empirically validated from iteration_25
outer layer bounds [100, 400] nm accommodate QWOT variations
theory_basis: Defective DBR structure (HL)^N D(LH)^N creates transmission peak at defect mode wavelength
Quarter-wave optical thickness n*d = lambda/4 provides maximum reflectance in stopbands
L2 curvature penalty reduces high-frequency thickness oscillations that cause fabrication sensitivity
expected_advantages: Reduced optimization dimensionality (12 vs 20 free parameters) improves convergence
Stopband QWOT initialization provides stronger initial suppression
Fixed core eliminates compensatory overshoot observed in iteration_25 candidates
known_risks: Fixed 215.0 nm may not be optimal for all stopband configurations
QWOT at 1450 nm may underperform at 1550 nm passband if mirrors are too reflective
Curvature penalty weight requires tuning to avoid over-constraint
execution_request_english: Design a 20-layer alternating Ta2O5/SiO2 bandpass filter on fused silica substrate with air incident medium. Layers 1-7 and 18-20 are optimization variables initialized at quarter-wave optical thickness for 1450 nm wavelength (Ta2O5 QWOT ≈ 1450/(4*n_H), SiO2 QWOT ≈ 1450/(4*n_L)) with ±10% random perturbation. Layers 8-17 are fixed constants at exactly 215.0 nm. Optimization bounds for free layers: [100, 400] nm. Apply L2 curvature penalty to objective function penalizing adjacent-layer thickness differences exceeding 30 nm. Evaluate coherent TMM across 1300-1800 nm. Score three weighted objectives: (1) transmittance at 1550 nm, (2) mean transmittance in 1400-1500 nm, (3) mean transmittance in 1600-1700 nm. Total layer count: exactly 20 layers. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1400-1500 nm, 1550-1550 nm, 1600-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance at 1550 nm (soft target ≥ 0.95); strong suppression of transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 1400-1500 nm; transmittance in 1600-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30.
revision_reason: Refines iteration_25 frozen-core approach by initializing outer layers at stopband QWOT (1450 nm) instead of arbitrary values, and adding explicit L2 curvature penalty to suppress compensatory overshoot observed in candidates 1-3 of iteration_25.
